findings.description: The plan requires exact commands for Firebase deploy and realtime smoke ActionItems, but the shipped ActionItem constructor validates exact_command against the known DontPanic command vocabulary. The plan does not say whether those external Firebase commands become validated operator-only commands, wrapper commands, or a new validated command class, so the catalog can fail at construction or silently lose the exact command outcome.

Adding SOURCE_INTEGRATION and provide_integration_actions() is not enough to prove the standard operator surfaces render the items. The shipped dashboard collection path explicitly aggregates each provider and maintains per-source scope and freshness maps; the plan does not require wiring the new provider through that real collect_state/dashboard.build/write_cache path.

F002 says the static smoke captures run output as an evidence ref, while F004 consumes evidence refs to flip status, but no feature pins the evidence storage location, schema, write API, or clears_when predicate input. Without that contract, the smoke can pass and still fail the completion test requiring status to change without hand-editing.

F004's description correctly says there is no separate integrations panel and status must route through shipped what-now/operator-console surfaces, but its steps still instruct implementation to render a dashboard integrations panel. That contradicts the objective contract and can lock a UI path the source-of-truth decision explicitly removed.

The plan names statuses configured, deployed, smoke-passing, and pending, but it does not pin the per-integration matrix mapping catalog entries and evidence refs to each status. Firebase, static dashboard, Linear, and Discord have different evidence shapes, so two implementations could satisfy the prose while linking or clearing different pending items.

F003 says deploy and realtime-smoke items render gated or unavailable until trigger and credentials are present, but the trigger source and credential-presence semantics are not pinned. That leaves room for hiding gated items, probing real secrets, or making visibility depend on live environment state, all of which conflict with offline fixture proof and no-secret rendering.

F002 says the static smoke verifies exported artifacts are present and parseable, but the journey and completion test require proof that the static dashboard actually renders those artifacts. Parseable JSON can still fail the dashboard loader or render path, so this can pass while missing the user-facing outcome.

The plan depends on operator-attested integration-evidence records to meet Firebase trigger conditions and clear external deploy, realtime smoke, Linear, and Discord items, but it does not define a user-facing capture path for those attestations. Without an explicit offline command or workflow, operators may have to hand-edit evidence files, contradicting the no-hand-editing resolution contract.

F004 says resolved integrations clear via clears_when while also promising configured, deployed, and smoke-passing readiness at a glance through existing what-now/operator-console surfaces. Because there is no separate integrations panel, the plan must pin what remains visible after pending ActionItems clear; otherwise successful integrations can disappear instead of surfacing their derived status.

The plan introduces operator_command, credentials_required, evidence_expected, and trigger_condition, but the shipped ActionItem envelope and dashboard normalizers currently use a closed set of serialized fields and source labels. F001 requires real rendering, but does not explicitly require these new display fields to survive ActionItem.to_dict, triage, what-now, and operator-console normalization.

The status matrix says stale or failed evidence keeps the integration at its prior floor, but the evidence contract is a JSON file per integration and does not define how prior successful evidence is preserved when a later failed record is written. Two implementations could overwrite success, silently regress, or ignore failure while still matching the current prose.

The plan requires exact credential requirements, but the proposed catalog mostly pins credentials_required as a boolean and does not lock the per-item env-var name list or display shape. Without a deterministic list of credential names, offline fixture checks and operator-facing setup guidance can pass while still failing to tell the operator what credentials are required.

F003 says gated Firebase deploy and realtime-smoke items always render, while F004 says only genuinely pending integrations occupy the needs-action band. The plan does not pin the band/status behavior for unmet triggers, so an implementation could either hide the item or incorrectly show not-yet-needed Firebase work as needing action.

F002 tests the smoke writer and F004 tests status derivation with fixtures, but the plan does not require the completion-test path where the rendered static-dashboard ActionItem exact_command is executed, writes evidence, and then the real provider-to-render rebuild flips that integration's status without hand-editing.
